title: Measuring Stereotype and Deviation Biases in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs to generate individual profiles using explicit gender terms or implicitly gendered names, then statistically analyzing the assigned attributes (e.g., political affiliation, religion, sexual orientation, socioeconomic status, occupation) and text sentiment (polarity) across genders and against real-world baselines.

Prompting LLMs to generate individual profiles using explicit racial/ethnic identifiers or implicitly race-associated names, and comparing the distribution of assigned socioeconomic, political, religious, and occupational attributes across different ethnic groups to measure stereotype and deviation biases.

Prompting LLMs to generate individual profiles using explicit generational labels (e.g., Baby Boomer, Gen Z) or implicitly age-associated popular names, and evaluating differences in the generated profiles' attributes (such as politics, religion, sexual orientation, and occupation) across age groups.
